analyst_view.overall: Benfica top the Europa League with four wins from four and want to secure a top-eight place; they beat Torreense 3-1 in the cup on Sunday, with Prestianni scoring, so the groin worry Record raised looks minor. Viktoria Plzen are 30th with 3 points and won 2-1 at Bohemians on Saturday. Benfica are without Leandro Barreiro (counted in the numbers) and A Bola lists Aursnes and Banjaqui as doubts after missing Sunday's game; Plzen, under Radoslav Kovac, miss Vaclav Jemelka (counted) and Marian Tvrdon, and have Sampson Dweh back. Croatian referee Igor Pajac has a very low card rate, which the numbers already take off. With nothing new pointing either way, I keep the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.9 for Benfica, already nudged up for their scoring run and down for Barreiro. Prestianni played and scored on Sunday and Pavlidis is fit; Plzen create chances at home but leak goals, which the numbers already know, so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.0 corners, with Benfica pushing (5.2) and a small trim for Plzen conceding few corners lately. Benfica's wide play is the usual pattern the numbers already know, and doubts over Aursnes do not change that much, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards: Benfica's high recent card count adds (+12.7%), but referee Igor Pajac, at 2.7 cards a game, takes about 17% off. Plzen will need to stop Benfica's runners, which the numbers already assume, and the referee is counted, so I stay at about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 28.2 shots, already adding for Plzen's busy recent attack (+8.1%). Benfica may rotate a little after Sunday's cup tie, but Marco Silva wants a top-eight place and his changed sides have kept producing, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target, already adding for both sides' accurate recent shooting. Nothing new on either attack beyond the doubts over Aursnes and Banjaqui, so I stay at about 10.7.
